In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the retrieval of mean Doppler velocities from space-borne radars, in particular from high frequency radars, is a very challenging task.
DOMUS, coupled to a WRF simulation, provides a very useful tool to study the retrieval of vertical hydrometeo motion using space-borne W-band Doppler radars, in particular for convective clouds.
DOMUS is capable of retrieving vertical hydrometer velocities in the convective clouds with a good accuracy, even in case of NUBF and multiple scattering.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the W-band Doppler radar has a good potential in retrieving vertical hydmeteor motions in convective clouds and that the NUBF and multiple scattering effects can be properly accounted for.

the Doppler radar is a very powerful tool to measure vertical motions of hyrometeors, however, it is very sensitive to the hydrometeor distribution, and it can provide very accurate results only when the beam is uniformly filled.
